text:
Vegas trailed Pittsburgh in the third period and still won. Tomas Hertl scored the winner on the power play with 35 seconds left, his second goal of the night, and the Golden Knights turned a game they were losing on the scoreboard into a 3-2 road win. Hertl, drafted 17th overall by San Jose in 2012, also scored the opening goal, a deflection on a first-period power play. Trevor Connelly, a 2024 first-round pick of Vegas, tied it at 2-2 at 11:19 of the third.

The play pointed the other way. Our expected goals model, which grades each shot by how often it scores, had Pittsburgh ahead 3.30 to 2.51 and gave the Penguins a 64% chance of winning if the game were replayed many times. At even strength the gap was wider, 2.27 to 1.22, and the Penguins outshot Vegas in attempts 56 to 40. They owned the third, 1.32 to 0.74 in expected goals, and Tommy Novak and Rickard Rakell scored on that pressure. Adin Hill is why it didn't count for more. He stopped 1.3 goals more than the shots he faced should have allowed, while Arturs Silovs allowed three on chances worth 2.51.

Special teams settled it. Vegas scored on two of its four power plays, Pittsburgh went 0 for 6, and both of Hertl's goals came with the man advantage. Pittsburgh lost the first meeting this season 6-2, so Vegas has now beaten the Penguins twice, though our numbers say this one was closer to a Pittsburgh game than the score suggests. Pittsburgh has the process to build on, and Vegas has the two points.
